  <h2 class="slide-title">Handheld-gripper data is scalable, but the embodiment gap blocks direct reuse.</h2>
  <p>UMI-style interfaces separate the teacher from the robot and replay demos directly<sup>[2]</sup>; FastUMI scales this<sup>[1]</sup>. Transfer fails when the executing end-effector differs from the handheld gripper<sup>[2][5]</sup>.</p>

<section class="slide">
  <h2 class="slide-title">FastUMI's 10k+ trajectories show depth and data scale improve transfer-relevant policies.</h2>
  <p>>10,000 real-world demos span 22 tasks, 19 object categories, 12 skills, ~6–12 s<sup>[1]</sup>; depth raises Diffusion Policy success 53.33→80.00% Pick Lid and 20.00→93.33% Open Ricecooker<sup>[1]</sup>; Pick Cup success 20.00/26.67/53.33% with 200/400/800 demos<sup>[1]</sup>.</p>
  <div class="slide-number">4</div>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2 class="slide-title">A different end-effector breaks geometry, actions, tracking, and mechanics.</h2>
  <p>Grasp geometry and contact points shift with shape and kinematics<sup>[5]</sup>; Diffusion Policy relative TCP poses do not by themselves handle embodiment<sup>[11]</sup>; T265 degrades under close-range occlusion and low light and may need reinitialization<sup>[1]</sup>; non-parallel jaws displace TCP, corrected by local-Z compensation<sup>[1]</sup>.</p>
  <div class="slide-number">5</div>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2 class="slide-title">The literature offers pooling, retargeting, policy/data fixes, and useful contrasts.</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Pool across embodiments: Open X-Embodiment<sup>[3]</sup>; RT-1<sup>[8]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Retarget mismatched hands: Doshi<sup>[5]</sup>; Sanches<sup>[6]</sup>; Dexcap<sup>[7]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Fix policy/data: Diffusion Policy<sup>[11]</sup>; Data Quality<sup>[12]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Contrasts: UMI<sup>[2]</sup>; human video<sup>[4]</sup>; VR teleop<sup>[9]</sup>; Grasping in the Wild<sup>[10]</sup>.</li>
  </ul>
  <div class="slide-number">6</div>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2 class="slide-title">Open problems: data quality, unsupported grippers, mismatched evaluation, sensing, and policy-first fixes.</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Re-annotate occluded/close-range recordings<sup>[1][12]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Retarget one unsupported gripper and measure the drop<sup>[1][5][6][7]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Evaluate mismatched end-effectors with per-task success<sup>[3][8][14]</sup>.</li>
    <li>Test tactile/force or wireless, and try depth/data first<sup>[1][11]</sup>.</li>
  </ul>
  <div class="slide-number">9</div>
</section>

<section class="slide">
  <h2 class="slide-title">Approve a 4-week pilot: clean data, build one retargeting baseline, evaluate mismatched transfer.</h2>
  <p>Week 1: clean/re-annotate occluded handheld recordings<sup>[1][12]</sup>. Weeks 2–3: retarget one gripper outside FastUMI's five attachments<sup>[1][5][6][7]</sup>. Week 4: Diffusion Policy on mismatched gripper; report per-task success drop<sup>[3][11][14]</sup>. Need: one unsupported gripper, compute, existing data.</p>
